# Protocol Checklist: The session never acts on a frame it could not parse

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the session-layer disposition of framed-but-unparseable frames (C-2 rows, sequence accounting, Reject contents, the inbound seqnum_max bound) against FIX-SL 2020 and the 2026-09-27 owner ruling on fixpp#507.
**Created**: 2026-09-27
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [contract](../contracts/unparseable-frame-disposition.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is a disposition defined for every combination of session state (NotConnected, LogonSent, LogonReceived, Active, LogoutSent, AwaitingResend), field-3-is-35, 34-read and MsgType class, with no combination falling through the C-2 table? [Completeness, Contract §C-2] — PASS: C-2 covers all six named states: D-1 NotConnected, D-2 LogonSent, D-9 LogoutSent (any field 3/34/35), and LogonReceived/Active are total over field-3 (D-8 no) → 34 read (D-7 no) → 35 value A/4/other × =/≠ expected (D-3..D-6); AwaitingResend is an Active sub-state (C-2 "D-4 during AwaitingResend", quickstart AwaitingResend D-5). Disconnected is outside the table by construction: its arm ignores every inbound frame with no scan (src/session/session.cpp `case fsm_state::Disconnected`, verified at a0878eab)
- [x] CHK002 Is the set of `hdr` fields a disposition may read on a faulty frame enumerated exhaustively (34, 35, the field-3 bit, and the fault kind / Length tag for the reason code), with every other field excluded? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Contract §C-3 I-1] — SPEC-FIXED: FR-001's exception listed only 34, 35 and the field-3 bit, while FR-007 fills 373/371 from the fault kind and Length tag; FR-001 now names the fault record (kind, Length tag) as readable only for 373/371 and `fault_offset` as never read, and contract C-3 I-1 enumerates the same set (spec.md FR-001; contract C-3 I-1)
- [x] CHK003 Are the Reject's field values (45, 372, 373, 371, 58) specified for every Reject row, including when 372 is omitted and when 371 is omitted? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, §FR-007, Contract §C-2] — PASS: contract C-2 "Reject contents (D-4, D-5, D-6)" fixes 45=fault_ref_seq_num, 372=fault_ref_msg_type omitted above the dictionary-derived bound (R-5), 373=0 with 371 omitted / 373=5 with 371=fault_length_tag, 58 fixed per kind; empty 372 omitted by build_reject_with_text (T016); FR-003, FR-007 agree
- [x] CHK004 Is the disposition of a faulty frame during AwaitingResend specified for each row, including a faulty GapFill (C-5 L-2) and a faulty in-sequence application message that fills the gap? [Completeness, Contract §C-2, §C-5 L-2] — PASS: C-2 rows are state-independent inside Active, and AwaitingResend is named where it differs: faulty GapFill → D-4, gap stays open, disclosed C-5 L-2 (cell T049); faulty in-sequence app filling the gap → D-5 via consume_rejected_seqnum_ → close_filled_resend_gap_ (C-2 D-5 note; quickstart AwaitingResend; T034) — verified consume_rejected_seqnum_ calls close_filled_resend_gap_ at head
- [x] CHK005 Are the late parse sites defined by a derivation (command plus classification rule) rather than a list, and is the single action at every site fully specified (close mode, no Reject, which callback is suppressed)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016, Contract §C-6] — PASS: contract C-6 "Population" gives the grep command plus the provenance classification rule (peer bytes → late site; fixpp-built → not); one action: close(close_mode::terminal), no Reject, parse target's fromAdmin/fromApp suppressed, onLogout/earlier callbacks scoped out (FR-016, C-6, E-3, R3-005)
- [x] CHK006 Is every `check_inbound` caller's disposition of `store_seqnum_overflow` specified, including the return value of `on_inbound_frame` at Guard 4? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, Research §R-14] — PASS: R-14 "Callers" classifies every check_inbound caller: consume_rejected_seqnum_ takes Disconnected and returns the error (its 5 callers co_return c before the Reject — verified at head), Guard 4 tests overflow first and returns store_seqnum_overflow from on_inbound_frame, the two pre-Active Logon arms already Disconnect on any non-tolerated error (verified at head: the only session.cpp callers are these 4; no other src/include caller)
- [x] CHK007 Are the effects a late close cannot undo (Guards 2–3, the Guard 4 advance, the resend-gap close, liveness, the confirming Logout) listed, so no requirement implies they are rolled back? [Completeness, Contract §C-6] — PASS: contract C-6 "Effects already taken are not undone" lists Guards 2–3, the Guard 4 advance, the resend-gap close, the liveness refresh and the Logout handler's confirming Logout; R-4 "What a late close does not do" repeats it and quickstart "Late sites" forbids asserting their absence
- [x] CHK008 Is the replay classification of a stored frame whose scan read no 35 specified, with its fail-safe outcome (gap-fill, never resend)? [Completeness, Research §R-12] — PASS: research R-12 Decision: a stored frame whose scan read no 35 is not app_present and is gap-filled (fail-safe, as fixpp#424), with an admin-frame-fault-in-field-2 cell RED against stop-first without the guard (T015)

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK009 Is "34 read" defined precisely enough to classify `34=abc`, `34=0`, a 34 straddling the fault, and a duplicate 34 before the fault? [Clarity, Data-model §E-1, Spec §FR-006] — PASS: data-model E-1 "Rules": 34 read ⇔ parse_seqnum(fault_ref_seq_num) > 0; `34=abc`/`34=0` not read (D-7); fault_ref_seq_num is the first well-formed 34 written once; a 34 that is itself the faulting field is never assigned (scan returns on first fault, unassigned members empty); duplicate cell 34=99|35=D|34=2|9x9=1 → D-6 with 45=99 (quickstart Duplicates, T034)
- [x] CHK010 Is "field 3 is 35" defined for the case where field 3 is itself the faulting field, and where the scan faults before field 3? [Clarity, Data-model §E-1, Contract §C-2] — PASS: E-1 msg_type_is_third is false "when the third field is itself the faulting field, or when the scan faults before reaching it"; contract C-2 note sends the former to D-8 in LogonReceived/Active and D-1/D-2 refuse pre-Active whatever field 3 is
- [x] CHK011 Is the "failure point" defined as a byte position with an unambiguous rule for which fields lie "wholly before" it? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities] — PASS: spec Key Entities defines the failure point as the byte position of the first unparseable field; E-1 fault_offset = the faulting field's first byte and "a field read before the fault is exactly a non-empty member" (fields are contiguous, so starting before fault_offset ⇔ wholly before it)
- [x] CHK012 Is "disregard" defined as one named disposition and used with exactly that meaning everywhere (no Reject, no advance, no disconnect), with liveness stated as a separate rule? [Clarity, Spec §Terminology, Spec §FR-018] — SPEC-FIXED: the disregard definition is the three-part "no Reject, no advance, no disconnect", used with that meaning in D-7/D-8/D-9, FR-006, FR-015 and T026; liveness is a separate rule that applies to every faulty-frame row (FR-018, re-dispositioned after the Fable consult of 2026-09-27), stated beside the definition in spec.md §Terminology, the contract preamble and data-model.md
- [x] CHK013 Is the term "garbled" reserved for the four §4.5.2 framing criteria across spec, plan, contract and B&L text, with "framed but unparseable" used for 092's input? [Clarity, Spec §Terminology] — PASS: grep of the bundle for "garbled" finds it only for the §4.5.2 criteria (Terminology, Context ruling quote, D-8 "criterion 3"), quoted ruling text, and the R-13 rewrite of brain/components/session.md's misuse; FR-014/T070–T071 carry the B&L and brain rewrites; the input is called "framed but unparseable" throughout
- [x] CHK014 Is "the message would consume NextNumIn" defined by predicate (Guard 4, a #423 site, D-5, a pre-Active Logon), with the non-consuming cases named? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities, Contract §C-5 L-7] — PASS: spec Key Entities "Inbound sequence bound" gives the consuming predicate (Guard 4, a #423 site, D-5, a pre-Active Logon) and names the non-consuming cases (Reset-mode SequenceReset, D-4, D-6, disregard rows; A/4 at #423 sites — verified consume_rejected_seqnum_ returns before check_inbound for "A"/"4" at head); C-5 L-7 and SC-010 match
- [x] CHK015 Is the 372 bound defined by derivation from the shipped dictionaries rather than by a literal, with the omission rule stated? [Clarity, Research §R-5] — PASS: research R-5 "372": a named constant recomputed by a unit test from dictionaries/*.xml (T018), 372 omitted (empty) above it, cell asserting a Reject without 372 (T034)

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK016 Do FR-003–FR-006 and the C-2 row order agree for every case, including a faulty Reject(3) or Logout(5) and a faulty Logon while Active? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003–§FR-006, Contract §C-2] — PASS: C-2 evaluates D-8, D-7 before D-3..D-6, and FR-006 (disregard) and FR-009's last sentence (faulty Logon refused only when field 3 is 35 and 34 read) state the same precedence; FR-003 "every MsgType, including Reject(3) and Logout(5)" = C-2 "Any other includes 3 and 5"; D-3 (A) precedes the Reject rows as FR-003 "not a Logon"
- [x] CHK017 Is the supersession of the no-reject-loop rule scoped identically in spec FR-003, contract C-2, the Edge Cases and the planned `admin_messages.hpp` text (faulty frames only; well-formed Reject/Logout keep the exemption)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Contract §C-2] — SPEC-FIXED: the Edge Case scoped the surviving exemption to "fails validation" while contract C-2 and T030 say "validation or SendingTime"; code has the msg_type != 3/5 exemption at the validate gates and at Guard 3 (session.cpp, verified); spec.md §Edge Cases now reads "fails validation or SendingTime"
- [x] CHK018 Are the pre-Active rules (D-1/D-2 refuse whatever field 3 is) consistent with FR-008, FR-009 and the deferral of the pre-Active disregard to fixpp#514? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009] — PASS: FR-008 routes a faulty frame before Active to FR-009; FR-009 refuses "whatever its MsgType and whatever its third field" and defers the pre-Active disregard to fixpp#514; contract C-2 pre-Active bullet and O-1 (#507 comment 5856425788) agree; the refusal source comments verified at head (`No MsgType discrimination`, `out-of-scope admin`)
- [x] CHK019 Do FR-019's precedence over FR-003/FR-004 at seqnum_max and FR-013's persist-before-Reject ordering produce one unambiguous outcome for D-5 at seqnum_max? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-019] — PASS: FR-019 "At NextNumIn = seqnum_max this requirement takes precedence over FR-003 and FR-004. No Reject is sent, because the advance FR-013 orders first has failed"; contract C-2 "D-5 at the expected number = seqnum_max"; T026 D-5 co_returns the consume failure before the Reject — one outcome
- [x] CHK020 Is the FR-018 liveness rule consistent between Active and LogonReceived, and between the Reject rows and the disregard rows? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, Contract §C-2] — SPEC-FIXED (re-dispositioned 2026-09-27 after the Fable consult, owner-delegated): FR-018's earlier rule (Reject rows refresh) rested on a false premise and would have made a faulty frame refresh where its well-formed twin does not. FR-018 now says no faulty-frame row refreshes and 092 adds no writer; contract C-2 "Liveness", the Terminology, data-model, quickstart §1 and T026/T031 agree. The rule is identical in Active and LogonReceived (no refresh) and across Reject and disregard rows; the site is re-derived by the grep plus the read of every `co_return` before it
- [x] CHK021 Is `fault_ref_msg_type` (never the last-wins `msg_type`) the value named in every place that decides a row or fills 372? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Contract §C-2] — PASS: fault_ref_msg_type is the named value in contract definitions ("35 value"), the D-5 note (consume_rejected_seqnum_ call and 372), Reject contents, FR-003, FR-004, Clarifications R3-001 and T026; no bundle text routes a row or fills 372 from hdr.msg_type (grep)

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK022 Are requirements stated for a faulty frame whose MsgSeqNum is below expected, above expected, and equal to expected, each with and without PossDupFlag=Y? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §C-2 D-6] — PASS: Edge Cases cover below/above expected and PossDupFlag=Y ("disposition the frame as if the flag were absent"), C-2 D-5 (= expected) and D-6 (≠, "PossDup not consulted"); quickstart D-6 and T029 require too-low/too-high each with and without 43=Y; equal-with-43=Y is D-5 by the same as-if-absent rule
- [x] CHK023 Is the outcome defined for a faulty frame carrying a wrong CompID or BeginString before the fault? [Edge Case, Spec §Clarifications Q2] — PASS: Clarifications Q2 "No — Reject only" and Edge Case "Wrong CompID or BeginString" (FR-001, FR-002 ordering before identity guards); cell T029
- [x] CHK024 Is the precedence of the MaxMessageSize(383) guard over the disposition stated for an oversized faulty frame? [Edge Case, Contract §C-1 step 1b] — PASS: contract C-1 step 1b and FR-002 put the MaxMessageSize(383) guard before the disposition (reads only frame.size()); Edge Case and T034 cell (oversized faulty frame → Disconnected)
- [x] CHK025 Is the reason code defined when a frame has more than one malformed field? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases] — PASS: Edge Case "More than one malformed field: the first failure point decides FR-006 and the reason code"; E-1 stops at the first fault; T029 cell
- [x] CHK026 Is the resend-loop behaviour of the disregard rows disclosed as an outcome rather than left implicit? [Coverage, Contract §C-5 L-1, Spec §A-5] — PASS: contract C-5 L-1 discloses the disregard-row resend loop as a B&L row pinned by a cell (T049); spec A-5 states it can arise on the disregard rows
- [x] CHK027 Is a bound stated on the Reject exchange between two peers that each reject faulty Rejects? [Coverage, Contract §C-2 "A loop is bounded"] — PASS: contract C-2 "A loop is bounded": fixpp never Rejects a well-formed Reject, and each fixpp Reject answers one peer frame (1:1), with the reject-loop bound cell (quickstart; T030)
- [x] CHK028 Are the seqnum_max outcomes defined for every store kind, with the non-persistence of the SequenceReset jump stated as the reason both kinds behave alike? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019, Research §R-14] — PASS: FR-019 "holds with a persistent and a non-persistent store"; research R-14 "The wrap happens on a persistent store too" gives the reason (MessageStore has no counter setter, verified: store/retrieve/next_seqnum/reset only); SC-010 cells on memory and FileStore (T051/T052)
